Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T48/T48n2003.xml). Blue Cliff Record by Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄): Yuanwu Keqin says that a board-carrying fellow (擔板漢) often dies in the phrase.

Senses.Explanation: A comic epithet for a one-sided person: a fellow carrying a board and seeing only one side. The stock line says that Xu Six carries a board and sees only one side, while Baiyu Jingsi states directly that each party sees one side and is precisely a board-carrying fellow (各見一邊，正是擔板漢). In a case Baiyu raises, Muezhou Daozong calls to an addressee and applies the name when the man turns; Xuedou Chongxian and Huanglong Huinan then debate its application, and Baiyu judges their opposed comments one-sided. The label extends beyond that case. Dongshan Meixi Du says that learning without awakening is overbearing pride, whereas awakening without learning is a board-carrying fellow (有學無悟謂之增上慢，有悟無學謂之擔板漢). Zhe'an Jingfan applies it both to delight at a rich feast and fear in a thorn thicket, and elsewhere says that enumerating ranks, mysteries, divisions, reality, and expedients only makes such a fellow before asking how the matter can be raised whole (只成擔板漢，此事如何舉得全). Yuanwu Keqin says that a board-carrying fellow often dies in the phrase (若是擔板漢，多向句中死却). Zen bends a comic physical image into a public epithet for the person whom a record presents as fixed on one side or trapped in wording; the entry reports those attested applications without generalizing beyond them.

SearchAliases: carry snow to fill a well
Senses.Explanation: Carrying snow to fill a well is a recurrent comparison for ineffective effort, applied to talk, question-and-answer, sitting Chan, and other undertakings. Literally, "carry snow to fill a well" : the load melts while the well remains unfilled. Chan records use the concrete impossibility as a compact appraisal of ineffective religious display and effort. Baishan applies it separately to "pick it up and immediately use it", to question-and-answer exchanges in an enumeration beside "talking mysteries, drawing a cake to satisfy hunger", and to trying to pass through by silent stillness, contrasted with trying to state it in words as "proving a turtle to be a soft-shelled turtle". Tian'an calls sitting Chan like carrying snow to fill a well and rhymingly calls composing poetry kneading snow into a ball. Yinyuan pairs the phrase with trying to fill a net by blowing and says that even ages of such actions have no place. The Zen-specific use is a verdict applied not to an ordinary futile chore but to recognizable Chan-scene responses—silence, words, questions and answers, sitting, gestures, and other attempted displays.

Senses.Explanation: This is what something is in itself, especially when the records set it against what that thing does. In the Blue Cliff Record, the source-unnamed questioner asks Zhimen Guangzuo what prajna is in itself, and Zhimen answers, ‘a bivalve holds the bright moon’; the paired question about its function receives ‘a rabbit carries young.’ Huanglong Huinan reworks the pair as ‘a pile of shit’ and ‘worms in the pile.’ Sixin Wuxin gives the same counter-answer, Ying'an Tanhua answers with meeting without courtesy, and Eryin Mi answers with flowers opening and spring birds singing. Elsewhere Yunfeng answers with an arrow piercing a willow leaf, Fayun Datong Shanben says ‘join,’ Qixin Haiyin sends the assembly to the hall, Foyuan Chegang points to the waves raised as soon as the tongue moves, and Muchen Daomin offers a starless steelyard with iron at both ends. Thus the word names the constituting side of the distinction, but the masters repeatedly make that apparent request for an abstract essence answerable by a concrete scene, encounter, or directive.

Senses.Explanation: The body exposed in the golden wind is Yunmen Wenyan's compact answer to the public question, 'When the trees are bare and the leaves have fallen, what then?' Later masters repeatedly raise, criticize, and answer the case, while verse authors carry its autumn scene into frost, leaves, river, moon and wind. 'Golden wind' is thus the autumn wind in the phrase's observable scene; the Chan pressure lies in presenting total exposure as the immediate answer, without supplying an object hidden behind it.
